lines.text: Zophar the Naamathite calls Job's speech a stream of words and says Job claims to be pure in God's sight.
Zophar wishes God would speak against Job and says God exacts from Job less than his iniquity deserves.
Zophar says God's deep things are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave, and longer than the earth.
Zophar says no one can stop God from imprisoning Job, and that a witless man can become wise quickly.

wrong_details.wrong: a witless man can become wise quickly
wrong_details.true: a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man

lines.text: Zophar tells Job to put away the iniquity in his hand, and says the wicked will hope for their last breath.
